chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, who said, 'Al-Abbas ibn Musa al-Baghdadi narrated to me, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):'

An answer regarding the marriage sermon: All praise is for Allah, the Chosen for Praise, who singles it out for Himself, glorified by His Mention and exalted by His Command. We praise Him, not doubting in Him; we consider what we prepare as hope for its success and key to its gain, and we attain needs from Him through it. We seek guidance from Allah by the firmness of guidance, the bonds of security, and the resolutions of piety, and we seek refuge with Allah from blindness after guidance, and action in the straying paths of desire.

And I testify that there is no god except Allah, One, with no partner, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, a servant who did not worship anyone other than Him. He chose him with His Knowledge, and made him trustworthy over His Revelation, and a Messenger to His creation. So may Allah send blessings upon him and his family.

Thereafter, we have heard your speech, and you are the close relatives; we desire alliance with you, assist you in your needs, and cherish your brotherhood. We have accepted your intercessor's intercession, and we have married your suitor, stipulating that for her is from the dower what you mentioned. We ask Allah, Who established affairs by His Power, to make the outcome of this gathering of ours what He loves. Indeed, He is the Guardian of that and the Able over it.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended text for the Islamic marriage sermon according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi records the specific formula for the marriage sermon (Khutbat al-Nikah) as transmitted by Imam al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizing the theological foundation of marriage through praise of God and testimony of the Prophet’s prophethood. It highlights the juristic acceptance of the proposal and the agreed dower (Mahr), serving as a model for the verbal contract in Shia fiqh. The narration concludes with a supplication for divine facilitation, reflecting the spiritual dimension of the marital bond.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa who said, ‘Al Abbas Bin Musa Al Baghdady narrated to us, 
(It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>,

in answer to a sermon of the marriage: ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the Chosen for the Praise, sincerely for Himself<sup>saww</sup>, His<sup>azwj</sup> Mention being Glorified by Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and His<sup>azwj</sup> Command being Radiated by Him<sup>azwj</sup>. We<sup>asws</sup> Praise Him<sup>azwj</sup> without being in doubt. We<sup>asws</sup> see what we<sup>asws</sup> prepare hoping for its success and as keys to its benefits, and we<sup>asws</sup> attain the needs by it from His<sup>azwj</sup> Presence. And we<sup>asws</sup> seek Guidance of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> with the impeccable Guidance, and firm Security, and determined piety. And we seek Refuge with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> from the blindness after the Guidance, and the actions during straying desires.

And I<sup>asws</sup> testify that there is no god except for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, One, there being no associates for Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and I<sup>asws</sup> testify that Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> is His<sup>azwj</sup> servant and His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup>, a servant such that he<sup>saww</sup> never worshipped anyone apart from Him<sup>azwj</sup>. He<sup>azwj</sup> Chose him<sup>saww</sup> with His<sup>azwj</sup> Knowledge, and a trustworthy upon His<sup>azwj</sup> Revelation, and a Rasool<sup>saww</sup> to His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures. So, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Send His<sup>azwj</sup> Blessings upon him<sup>saww</sup> and his<sup>saww</sup> Progeny<sup>asws</sup>.

Thereafter, so we<sup>asws</sup> have heard your speeches, and you are the neighbours, the nearest ones we<sup>asws</sup> wish to be in your alliance, and assisting you in your needs, and desiring to be your brethren. So we<sup>asws</sup> have accepted the intercession of your interceders, and we<sup>asws</sup> hereby marry to your proposer upon a stipulation that for her would be from the dower what you have mentioned. We<sup>asws</sup> ask Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Who Endorsed the affairs with His<sup>azwj</sup> Measurement, that He<sup>azwj</sup> Makes the end result of this gathering of ours to be what He<sup>azwj</sup> Loves, Him<sup>azwj</sup> being the Guardian of that and the One Able over it’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa who has said that narrated to me al-‘Abbas ibn Musa al- Baghdadiy in a marfu’ manner has said the following:

“Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, as response in Khutbah for marriage has said, ‘All praise belongs to Allah who chooses praise especially for Himself, glorified is thereby His mention and facilitated thereby is His command. We praise Him without any doubt in it; we see what we prepare in the hope for success and as key to its benefit. We receive what we need from Him and we seek guidance from Allah, a safe guidance and strong means of safety and the determination for piety. We seek protection with Allah against blindness after guidance and against working in misleading desires.

I testify that no one other than Allah alone, who has no partners, deserves worship and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, a servant who never worshipped anyone other than Him. He chose him by His knowledge and entrusted him with His revelation, as a messenger to His creatures, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause.

Thereafter, we have heard your words and you are the nearest generation with whom we like to have marital relationship and assist you in your needs. We are greedy for your brotherhood. We have accepted the mediation of your mediator and given in marriage to the one from you who have proposed for marriage for the designated mahr (dower) and we ask Allah who decides all issues with His power to make the consequences of our meeting towards His love; He is the guardian thereof and has power thereat.’”
